chapter_title: Concerning the Four Great Days that have come forth from one another, together with the Four Nights
chapter_note: The chapter is dominated by a schematic cosmological taxonomy (four Days / four Nights, each with twelve ‘hours’) in an impersonal expository voice—strongly CORE. The only clear later intrusions are brief institutional/application anchors (“his church”, “sects”, “old man”) and the formulaic opening/closing benedictions. No explicit NT citation overlay appears.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue attribution (“Once again the enlightener speaks”) is hagiographic frame, not part of the substrate teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: The first great day is the Father, the God of truth, the fir[st ... ... m]idst the aeons of his greatness, in his [l]iving kingdom. The twelve hours of this great day are the twelve great rich Gods of greatness. These, who are the first evocations that he evoked (to mirror) his greatness, he spread out to the four climes, three by three before his face.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic degree-mapping within the cosmos (Day ↔ Father ↔ twelve hours ↔ twelve rich Gods ↔ four climes). Impersonal structural exposition marks CORE.

paragraphs.core_text: The second day is the Third Ambassador, the one who dwells in the light ship. His twelve hours are the twelve virgins that he evoked in his greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same internal cosmological mapping (Day ↔ cosmic entity ↔ twelvefold hypostases) with no institutional reach.

paragraphs.core_text: [The third day is the Pillar of Glory, the great porter that is greater than] all [the po]rters; the one that supports all [ ... ], those above and those below. Its twelve hours are the five sons of the First Man; the five sons of the Living Spirit, who support all the weights of the universe; together with the summons and the obedience, which are counted to their ten brethren. These are the twelve light hours of the third day.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmos→cosmos correspondential systematisation (Pillar / porter-function; pentads + summons/obedience making twelve). No exhortation or contemporary identifications.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth day is Jesus the Splendour. His twelve hours are the twelve wisdoms, which are his [light] h[o]u[rs].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the institutional locator “who [dwells in] his church” as an application/communal anchor (cosmos→community) interrupting an otherwise internal cosmological mapping.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The identification of the fourth Day with a cosmic being and a twelvefold set is CORE in form; “church” shifts the mapping outward to the community and is likely a later editorial application.
Summative benediction (“Blessed is every one…”) functions as editorial closure/exhortation rather than systematic exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ]: For just as four day[s ex]ist, s[o] too four nights exist.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief structural hinge introducing the matching fourfold Night taxonomy; remains within the system (days↔nights) without institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: The first night is the land of darkness. It has twelve black [shadows] therein, which are its dark h[o]ur[s]. The twelve shadows of the first night are the five elements of the land of darkness, [which] poured forth from its five sense organs; and [ ... ] which [ ... ] in its [fi]ve elements and its five [ ... ]; the five [sp]irits that dwell in its elements [ ... ]. These are the twelve shadows and spirits of the first night.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Internal dark-cosmos structuring (night↔realm↔twelve shadows/hours, grounded in pentadic elements/sense-organs) is characteristic CORE schematisation.

paragraphs.core_text: The second night is Matter, the sculptress [ ... ... ] who has sculpted [ ... ] and the entire ruling-power that is in the worl[ds of darkness]. She has fashioned it in five sense organs, five [male] and five female, two per world; together with the fire and the lust [that] dwell in men and women, inflaming [them] inward to one another. These are the twelve spirits of this second night.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-architectonic description of Matter’s structuring work (sense-organs, male/female, fire/lust) stays within the mythic system despite anthropological language.

paragraphs.core_text: Indeed she, this Matter, the thought of death, ga[ve] the King of the realms of Darkness and his powers strength for the war and the fight, against the aeons of greatness. Yet, he was caught! They laid a snare for him through the Fi[rst M]an. [He] was ta[ken] t[o ... ] through the powers [ ... He] was brought up from the land of death and s[et ... ab]ove and below in the [whole] universe; in the five par[t]s in the heavens above, as well as the five [parts] in the earths below; together with the heat and the cold that are the father and the mother, their fire and their l[u]st.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-cosmological process account (war, snare through First Man; cruciform emplacement above/below; pentadic heavens/earths) in impersonal narrative-exposition is CORE.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the second night that is begotten from the first night. They laid a snare for her through the First M[a]n. She was brought up by the hand of the Living Spirit, and set in this composite univers[e ... ] he[r], above and below. The [upper side is the sense] organs of males; the lower side [ ... ] fe[mal]es.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Genealogical unfolding (night-from-night) plus cosmic emplacement by the Living Spirit is internal system mechanics—CORE.

paragraphs.core_text: The thir[d night is the five] worlds of flesh [ ... five] male, and five female; that were begotten from the powers [abo]ve. They have fallen upon the earth, being displayed in wh[at is d]ry and what is moist; together with the fire and the lust [that d]we[l]l in them, which drives them inward to one another.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic pentadic structuring of the ‘worlds of flesh’ and elemental display (dry/moist) continues the internal cosmological taxonomy.

paragraphs.core_text: [Mat]te[r] herself, the thought of death, is the [mother] of them all; as among them she is named 'the night'. [The worlds] of male and female fleshes, together with the fire and the l[ust], shall [ ... ] twelve hours of [ ... ... ] night. Again, [it] too, the third night that is in the worlds of fl[e]sh, was begotten from the second night; which the Living [Spir]it crucified in the uni[verse ... , ab]ove and below in heaven [ ... ... ].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Reinforces the night-genealogy and cosmic ‘crucifixion’/fixation above-below; still a self-contained mythic mechanics layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth night is the law of Sin, which is the dark spirit who speaks in the twelve spirits. They are the nakedne[ss]es, the twelve zodiacal signs of Matter. They are her thrones;
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed “the twelve sects” and the concluding application clause (“…as she sculpts and is displayed in the old man”) as cosmos→contemporary/religio-anthropological pointing rather than cosmos→cosmos mapping.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Zodiacal/twelvefold structuring is CORE in style, but the explicit identification with “sects” (and the ‘old man’ application) shifts the correspondence outward and signals later editorial use.

paragraphs.core_text: And, also, the hours of this fourth night are the twelve e[vi]l spirits; the [ ... ] of the old man, which [are ... ... ... ... di]fferentiate the day and night [ ... ... of] death.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the appositive identification “that is the old man, who reigns in the sects” as institutional/application anchoring (cosmos→sects).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The twelvefold ‘evil spirits’ as hours continues the schema, but the editor anchors it polemically to “sects”; the remaining line still carries some anthropological residue (‘old man’), so extraction is conservative.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the fourth night [ ... ] that have come forth of one another. One has [ ... ... ] just like the days of lig[ht ... ] they manifested one another. So als[o ... ] they did arise out of one another.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Structural recap in the same schematic voice (nights arising from one another) without institutional or citation markers—CORE.
Closing beatitude/exhortation (“Blessed is he…”) functions as editorial devotional closure rather than the cosmological schema itself.
